title: Fundamental Principles
context: Delhi AYUSH describes Vata, Pitta and Kapha as traditional doshas. In this account, Vata concerns movement; Pitta concerns digestion and metabolism; Kapha concerns cohesion, lubrication and stability. These are descriptions within Ayurvedic theory.
context_kind: Original short paraphrase checked against publisher page
review_notes: Restricted to traditional functional descriptions. Excluded causal disease assertions and biomedical equivalences. No diagnosis inferred.

examples.question: How do the three doshas differ in this account?
examples.answer: Vata concerns motion, Pitta the processing of food, and Kapha structural support; the passage presents traditional roles [1].

examples.question: Does Pitta have the same role as Kapha here?
examples.answer: No. The account links Pitta to digestive processing and Kapha to holding structures together and supporting stability [1].

examples.question: Is movement assigned to Pitta in this passage?
examples.answer: The passage assigns motion to Vata; it instead places digestion and metabolism within the traditional description of Pitta [1].

examples.question: What laboratory test measures these doshas?

title: Prakriti

review_notes: Excluded the page's disease predictions, lifespan assertions and personal dietary recommendations. Categories are traditional classifications, not personal assessments.

examples.question: Does Prakriti describe only physical appearance?
examples.answer: No. This traditional account includes psychological temperament as well as physical constitution, so appearance alone does not exhaust its definition [1].

examples.question: Is a two-dosha constitution excluded by this description?

title: Ayurvedic Medicine: In Depth
context: NCCIH describes Ayurveda as an Indian traditional medical system involving products, diet, exercise and lifestyle. Products may include plant, animal, metal or mineral ingredients. context_kind: Original short paraphrase checked against publisher page
review_notes: General evidence and product-risk statements only. No individual treatment decisions or blanket assertion that all products are harmful.

examples.question: Is Ayurveda only the use of plant products?
examples.answer: No. This account includes food, activity and lifestyle, and describes ingredients that are not necessarily derived from plants [1].

examples.question: Do preliminary trials establish effectiveness for every condition?
examples.answer: No. Small samples and weak designs limit conclusions; the passage does not establish effectiveness across all health conditions [1].

examples.question: Does traditional use establish that every preparation is safe?
examples.answer: No. NCCIH identifies potentially toxic metals in some preparations, so traditional use alone does not establish universal safety [1].

examples.question: Which brand has no contamination?
